transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-01-06
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood), Marcus Lee (QuantaHealth - Head of Platform), Elena Ortiz (Cloud Security), Devon Park (Infra), Avery Wood (ML)

Summary: quick sync on network tasks, recent benchmark numbers, and upgrade scheduling.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick off real quick. this is our weekly POC checkpoint for the private vpc pilot. i think we have a fairly short agenda, networking updates from devon and elena, then liam will share the perf numbers and propose the upgrade plan.

[00:27] Marcus: sounds good, thanks. 

[00:33] Elena: quick note on timing — we need the SOC2 artifacts for any private deployment before we can move to production, just a reminder.

[00:40] Samira: absolutely, i'll put those in the thread today. liam, over to you for the numbers.

[00:48] Liam: yeah, thanks. quick context — we pushed the tuned batching config last week and enabled prefix KV cache persistence. initial results look promising: p50 on the 2k token workload is about 95ms, p95 is 180ms, p99 around 220ms for the quantized 13B model on the dedicated pilot nodes. cache hit rate increased from about 11% to 42% after the prefix caching changes.

[01:20] Avery: nice — is that for the default batch size or the tuned smaller batch?

[01:25] Liam: the tuned smaller batch, we reduced batch windows from 60ms to 30ms for latency-sensitive paths, and that helped p95. for throughput runs we kept larger windows and saw better token/second.

[01:40] Devon: curious — were those runs with ephemeral NAT egress? we noticed some variance when traffic went through the shared NAT.

[01:48] Liam: yes, the last runs used your staging NAT. variability is mostly at the egress layer when external model downloads or telemetry hit the internet. that's why we recommended a static egress IP or forwarding through a dedicated NAT.

[02:05] Marcus: we can create a dedicated NAT gateway, but we need the list of egress IPs that redwood will use so we can whitelist them.

[02:12] Samira: we'll provide the ip block list; liam i'll let you add that to the action items.

[02:18] Elena: also firewall rules — currently our fw team flagged that the instance profile needs fewer open ports; can we confirm only 443/22 (limited) are needed and document any internal ports redwood uses for health checks?

[02:30] Priya: yeah, normal TLS on 443, ssh only for support with jumpbox. health checks between nodes use 8080 internally but traffic shouldn't come from outside the VPC. we'll document everything.

[02:45] Devon: i'll post screenshots of the route table and security group after the call.

[02:50] Samira: perfect. liam, can you walk upgrade plan?

[02:56] Liam: sure — we're proposing runtime v2.3.1 which contains improved kvcache persistence and compatibility with the new compilation kernels. prereqs: nodes should be on kernel 5.10+ and docker runtime 24.x, python 3.10 on the control plane. upgrade is non-disruptive for most paths but we request a 2-hour maintenance window to run canary deploys and quick rollbacks if needed.

[03:20] Marcus: any expected downtime for in-flight requests?

[03:24] Liam: no full downtime; we rely on horizontal rolling restarts. short tail latencies can spike briefly during node handovers, which is why we want the window for careful verification.

[03:35] Avery: would this affect our kv cache warmup? we saw cold start latencies yesterday on a scaled test.

[03:42] Liam: warmup might be impacted for the initial canary nodes, but the new persistence should rehydrate faster. we're also planning to pre-warm key prefixes during the canary.

[03:55] Elena: we need the upgrade playbook and rollback steps to be attached to the ticket. security wants runbooks for each step.

[04:03] Liam: absolutely, i'll draft the playbook and include rollback, checking points, and logs to collect.

[04:10] Marcus: on the networking front, devon — any blockers?

[04:14] Devon: two small blockers: 1) we don't yet have the finalized egress ip list from redwood to whitelist, 2) route propagation between our transit gateway and the pilot vpc needs one more static route to point to the dedicated nat. after those are in place we can run full load tests.

[04:36] Samira: we'll get the ip list today. elena, any compliance concerns beyond SOC2? data residency?

[04:44] Elena: mostly key management — we need KMS integration with our HSM for key wrapping. is that supported in private mode?

[04:50] Priya: yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; we'll send the integration doc and a sample terraform snippet.

[04:59] Marcus: great. about benchmarks — avery, can you summarize what you ran this week?

[05:04] Avery: ran the quantized 13B model across 1k/2k/5k token slices. latency numbers per liam's summary are consistent. throughput at 5k token batch was ~1.1 tokens/ms for the node shape we're using. memory stayed within expected limits after the new quant profile. i uploaded a couple graphs to the shared spreadsheet.

[05:28] Devon: did you hit any OOMs during the high-traffic test? we saw one instance restart yesterday.

[05:34] Avery: that restart coincided with an un-evicted model load during a memory spike; we've adjusted the eviction thresholds and haven't seen repeats in the last 24 hours.

[05:46] Marcus: are you comfortable with the model versions pinned for the pilot or do you recommend a different variant for lower cost?

[05:53] Liam: for the pilot we recommend the quantized 13B as it hits a good balance of latency and quality. we can test a 7B quant for cheaper egress and throughput, but will likely see a quality delta on the longer context cases.

[06:10] Samira: quick cross-check on procurement — when we move to dedicated, procurement will need the license and estimated monthly commit. we can put together a draft estimate after the throughput test.

[06:20] Marcus: okay.

[06:23] Elena: another security flag — audit logs. do we capture request-level logs and can you push them to our splunk?

[06:30] Priya: yes, audit logs are available and we can forward to splunk via syslog or push to an s3 bucket you control; we'll include configuration steps.

[06:41] Devon: for the egress ip list — any chance redwood can provide a small CIDR block rather than dozens of ips? simplifies our ACLs.

[06:48] Samira: we'll ask the infra team; if not possible we'll provide a concise list.

[06:55] Liam: quick note on routing — if you use transit gateway attachments make sure the route table has explicit 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT and we recommend disabling source/dest checks on the jumping nat instance.

[07:10] Marcus: noted.

[07:15] Samira: okay, action items recap — samira will send SOC2 and network doc; liam will produce upgrade playbook; devon will post route table screenshots; avery will run throughput tests. anything else?

[07:30] Marcus: one more — can you add expected cost delta for quantized 13B vs 7B? procurement wants ballpark.

[07:38] Samira: yes we'll add that to the estimate after the throughput test.

[07:45] Elena: also please include the encryption-at-rest details — which keys are customer-managed and how access is auditable.

[07:52] Priya: we'll include KMS/HSM flow diagrams.

[08:00] Liam: quick follow-up on the performance: we also saw that enabling partial KV caching for prompt prefixes improved token efficiency by roughly 8% across the set tasks. that translates to measurable cost savings in the pilot.

[08:15] Avery: can you quantify — like tokens saved per 1k requests?

[08:20] Liam: rough back-of-envelope: around 80-120 tokens saved per 1k requests depending on prompt reuse patterns. we'll add exact numbers in the spreadsheet.

[08:33] Marcus: that's useful.

[08:36] Devon: timeline for the upgrade window? you mentioned 2 hours. can we aim for 2027-01-14?

[08:42] Liam: yes that date looks good; propose 02:00-04:00 UTC to minimize user impact.

[08:48] Marcus: we'll tentatively hold that window on our calendar, pending the route/egress checklist.

[08:55] Samira: i'll create the calendar invite once we agree on final time.

[09:00] Elena: one procedural question — during the upgrade will there be extra log verbosity? we need to ensure no sensitive data leaks into logs.

[09:07] Priya: we will not increase PII or request payload logging. the suggested logs are metrics, health checks, and performance traces with identifiers only.

[09:15] Marcus: good.

[09:18] Liam: last technical thing — kernel/module compatibility. some of your nodes are on an older kernel image; the upgrade expects 5.10+. devon, can you check node kernel versions and confirm?

[09:28] Devon: i'll check and post results. i think one node is still 4.x from an older AMI.

[09:33] Samira: if needed we can coordinate a short AMI rebuild or skip that node from the canary set.

[09:40] Devon: we'll aim to have all nodes at 5.10 by 2027-01-12.

[09:47] Avery: on the ML side, i'll try the 7B quant variant and post quality diffs on longer context cases to the sheet.

[09:55] Liam: great — that'll help procurement decisioning.

[10:00] Samira: ok we're about halfway through the agenda but this is going well. any other blockers from customer side?

[10:06] Elena: not besides what's listed.

[10:10] Marcus: no.

[10:13] Samira: cool — let's go through final recap and next steps.

[10:18] Samira: recap: redwood will send SOC2 + network docs, provide egress IP list, liam will write upgrade playbook, avery to run throughput tests and try 7B quant variant, devon to post route table screenshots and confirm kernel versions, and we tentatively schedule the upgrade for 2027-01-14 02:00-04:00 UTC.

[10:40] Marcus: yep, thanks everyone.

[10:44] Samira: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with attachments and the calendar invite.

[10:50] [meeting ends]
